notes:
Dedicated capacity sizing workshop — CRM summary and raw notes:
- Company: Riverbend Reserve, consulting firm building inference-backed routing + match/rerank layers for enterprise search products.
- Primary ask: reserved GPU pool with throughput guarantees and clear latency SLOs; must support steady-state and sustained peaks without user-visible degradation.
- Workload profile (workshop capture): steady-state baseline = 8 QPS of generation traffic (chat/rerank mix), median request = 180 tokens, peak burst profile = up to 220 QPS over 5-10 minute windows (marketing blast / nightly re-rank).
- Tokens: estimate avg tokens/response 180 -> raw token demand during steady-state ~1440 tokens/sec (~8*180); peak token demand ~39,600 tokens/minute (~660 tokens/sec) during 220 QPS if responses are similar length. Client asked for conversion to tokens/sec and GPU sizing guidance.
- Latency targets: generation p95 target = 350ms for 256-token responses; end-to-end p95 (app-side) target = 700ms. Cost sensitivity: medium-high (wants predictable unit economics).
- Routing/fallback: require automatic fallback to smaller quantized model if primary pool saturated; multi-region redundancy (NA primary, EU failover) required for sales/legal.
- Security: must support SSO (SAML), KMS integration for keys, audit logs with 1-year retention, and option for on-prem/offline mode for select customers.
- Recommended architecture (workshop output, preliminary):
  * Primary reserved pool (NA): 6 x H100-80GB nodes for the main chat/rerank workload to meet p95 SLOs at steady + burst with batching and KV cache.
  * Secondary regional failover (EU): 2 x H100-80GB hot-standby + autoscale burst to cloud for extreme events.
  * Embeddings/async workloads: 4 x L4 (or equivalent) in a separate pool for vectorization and high-concurrency low-latency embed calls.
  * Policy: workload-aware routing -> chat to H100 pool, short embed/rerank to L4; can spill to quantized variants for degraded perf.
- SLA asks: 99.9% uptime for dedicated pool, defined throughput guarantee (QPS and tokens/sec) per model family, credits for breach. Legal wants specifics on data residency and incident notification windows.
- Cost estimate range shared in deck (drive:/sales/riverbend/sizing-deck-v2.pdf); client wants line items broken down by GPU-hours, support tier, observability retention.
- Client quote: "We need predictable tail latency during our marketing spikes or the customer experience drops off — that's non-negotiable."
- Open questions from workshop: exact distribution of requests across models (chat vs rerank vs embeddings), expected concurrency per user session, retention window for KV-caches, acceptable fallback quality loss.
- PoC acceptance criteria proposed: 1) sustain 180 QPS for 10 minutes with p95 generation <= 350ms; 2) failover test to EU with <500ms additional latency; 3) automated routing to quantized fallback when primary utilization >85%.
- Next actions: provide revised sizing deck with three scenarios (conservative, expected, aggressive); run synthetic PoC with Redwood test harness; legal to circulate term sheet with residency addendum.
- Short fragments: "need canary rules for model rollouts", "cost per token breakdown at 95th pct", "verify KV cache warmup times", "SE to run H100 vs L4 bench by 2025-02-28"
